readerContract.humanQuestion: I keep revising a prompt, but how do I know whether the new version is actually better?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: The reader leaves with a small repeatable comparison she can run after every bounded prompt revision.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: She can write and revise prompts but may judge improvement from one fresh answer, a smoother tone or a different example.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A prompt revision is an experiment: keep representative examples and pass criteria stable, change one thing and compare the same results again.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: The same comparison works for a repeated workplace summary and a repeated at-home planning task.
readerContract.surfaceJob: One playful, current and source-backed prompting habit that fits the compact Promptoscope service card.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can stop endless prompt fiddling and tell when a revision genuinely helped.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: You cannot judge a prompt revision fairly if the task and success test change at the same time.
causalSequence: A fresh example can make a weak revision look better by chance.
Keeping representative examples and pass criteria stable creates a fair comparison.
Changing one instruction and rerunning the same cases shows whether the revision fixed, preserved or broke required behavior.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A communications lead compares the same fictional meeting-note summaries after one instruction changes.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A home cook compares the same invented-cupboard meal plans after one instruction changes.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Save representative examples, write down what good must include, change one instruction and rerun the same examples.

analogyPlan.concept: A revision can introduce a regression.
analogyPlan.mapping: Regression means the new version loses behavior the old version passed; Mercury supplies the horoscope misdirection.
analogyPlan.limit: Planets do not cause or diagnose prompt behavior.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: It turns a technical testing term into a memorable Promptoscope landing without hiding the definition.

humourPlan.lessonJob: Mercury takes the false blame only after the reader sees the actual cause: a revision failed an old check.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Forecast headline; one test sequence; paired work/home examples; explicit regression definition; short horoscope landing.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No generic context tip, magic wording or list of prompt ingredients; one repeatable comparison owns the card.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Answer first, make the hidden comparison visible through two familiar tasks, then land the regression joke after defining it.

usefulCuriosity.reason: A smoother answer can hide a lost requirement.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: The card contrasts tone improvement with a failed old case.

familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: Both settings rerun invented examples after one change.

limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: The card says a few representative examples, not proof of universal reliability.

humourSurprise.reason: The horoscope format can carry the regression concept without mysticism.
humourSurprise.plannedEvidence: Mercury is declared innocent after the failed check is identified.

betterNextQuestion.reason: More revisions is the wrong goal.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: The replacement question is whether the new version still passes the same useful cases.

explanationArc.adaptation: A service card compresses the arc into one usable move and routes depth to the class.

explanationReasoningDesign.humanEntry: A reader has revised the same prompt repeatedly and cannot tell whether the latest version is actually better.
explanationReasoningDesign.fakeUnderstandingRisk: She may mistake one polished new answer for evidence that the workflow improved overall.
firstPrinciplesSequence: Different examples can produce different results even when the prompt does not improve.
Stable examples and criteria make versions comparable.
One bounded change reveals which revision caused a pass or regression.
explanationReasoningDesign.explainBackTest: Explain why a smoother new meeting summary can still be a worse prompt result.
explanationReasoningDesign.transferCase: Apply the same comparison to a home meal-planning prompt using the same invented cupboard cases.
explanationReasoningDesign.usefulLanding: Change one thing, rerun the same examples and keep the new version only if it still meets the job.
explanationReasoningDesign.rewindEraAdaptation: The horoscope voice falsely suspects Mercury, then returns causality to the observed regression; the joke performs the teaching job.

evidenceAnalysis.claimUnderInspection: A prompt is better because one new answer sounds smoother after several revisions.
evidenceAnalysis.establishes: OpenAI recommends representative tasks, one bounded prompt/tool change at a time and rerunning the same evaluations.
evidenceAnalysis.doesNotEstablish: That a tiny test set proves universal reliability or that one prompt will stay best across future models and tasks.
evidenceAnalysis.claimedImpact: Another wording change improved the repeated workflow.
evidenceAnalysis.realConsequence: The reader can compare versions more fairly and detect when a revision loses an earlier requirement.
evidenceAnalysis.aidbReason: A repository search of recent AIDB records on August 11 found no conflicting treatment of this exact prompt-evaluation habit; current official OpenAI guidance supplies the product truth.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Producing another generic Promptoscope that merely says add context or try better wording.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: The exact card must give a repeatable before-and-after method, paired work/home examples and a regression decision.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A newcomer can explain why changing one thing and rerunning the same examples is more informative than judging one polished answer.
